record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: If c > 1 is nonintegral, is the integer sequence [n^c] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence for arbitrary commuting transformations? More specifically, for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, does the L^2-limit of (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{[n^c]}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{[n^c]}fℓ exist and equal the L^2-limit of the linear averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ?

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Show that if c > 1 is not an integer, then the sequence ([n^c]) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of commuting transformations. Moreover, show that if (X, X , µ, T1, . . . , T`) is a system and f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ), then the L^2(µ)-limit limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^[n^c]f1 · · · T`^[n^c]f` is equal to the L^2(µ)-limit limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^n f1 · · · T`^n f`.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $c>1$ be a non-integer real number, and write $[\,\cdot\,]$ for the integer-part (floor) function. Let $\ell\geq 1$, and let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ be a measure-preserving system, meaning $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a probability space and $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$ are commuting measure-preserving transformations of $X$. For bounded measurable functions $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the averages
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^{[n^c]}f_1 \cdot T_2^{[n^c]}f_2 \cdots T_\ell^{[n^c]}f_\ell$$
and
$$B_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^{n}f_1 \cdot T_2^{n}f_2 \cdots T_\ell^{n}f_\ell.$$

Prove the following two statements:

(i) (Multiple recurrence) The sequence $([n^c])_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is good for multiple recurrence for commuting transformations; that is, for every such system and every $A\in\mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{-[n^c]}A\cap T_2^{-[n^c]}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{-[n^c]}A\bigr)>0.$$

(ii) (Multiple convergence) The $L^2(\mu)$-limit $\lim_{N\to\infty} A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$ exists, and is equal to the $L^2(\mu)$-limit $\lim_{N\to\infty} B_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Norm convergence of linear multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations is known (Tao, 2008). For fractional iterates $[n^c]$ with $c>1$ non-integer, results exist only for a single transformation or for random/Hardy-field variants; the deterministic case with arbitrary commuting transformations appears to remain open as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Norm convergence of multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations
status_evidence.snippet: Multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations T_1,...,T_l converge in L^2 for linear iterates.
status_evidence.claim: The linear (n-th power) case is solved for commuting transformations, providing the baseline for comparison.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic averages for sparse corners
status_evidence.snippet: Results have been proven for random versions of [n^c], while the deterministic versions where one replaces a_n with [n^c] remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The deterministic fractional-power case for commuting transformations is reported as still open.
